Well, doctor, honestly, I’m just here because I am at my absolute wit’s end trying to get someone, anyone, to actually listen to me and understand what’s been going on. For months now—and I mean literally months—I’ve been trying to explain to people that my husband’s family, his side of the family, is quietly, just very underhandedly, messing with our money and our good name. 

I know people think I'm making a mountain out of a molehill, but I see the proof everywhere. I've been a billing clerk for a long time, so I know numbers, I know when things don't line up. And lately, these little billing errors keep showing up at my work... just tiny discrepancies that someone who isn't paying attention might just brush off as a mistake, but I see them. I know what they mean. 

And it's not just the finances, it's our reputation, too. I'll go to church on Sunday, and suddenly someone I've sat next to for years is acting funny toward me, giving me these strange looks, or cutting a conversation short for no reason at all. And people tell me I'm overthinking it, they pull up the bank records or the office logs and say, look, everything is fine, it's just a typo, but they don't see the whole picture. No matter what records anyone pulls up, no matter what paperwork they try to show me, I know for a fact it all ties back to his family pulling strings behind the scenes to ruin us. They're just very, very careful about hiding it, but I know exactly what they're doing.

That is exactly the problem, doctor, and it is exactly why I'm sitting here today. I know it does. They are quietly messing with our money and our good name, and they are doing it so meticulously, so underhandedly, that everyone else just thinks I'm overreacting or seeing things that aren't there. Change my mind? Doctor, I honestly don't know what else to tell you, and I really feel like a broken record here. I feel like I'm just repeating myself over and over, because what new information could there possibly be that would just erase everything I've been living through? 

Like I've been saying this whole time, I am here because for months now I’ve been trying to get people to understand that my husband’s family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. That is the reality of my life. So if you're asking if some piece of paper is going to change my mind, the answer is absolutely not. Because no matter what records anyone pulls up—and believe me, my supervisor has pulled up every spreadsheet, every batch file from the last three quarters, and my husband has practically wallpapered the dining room table with our bank statements trying to prove me wrong—I know it ties back to them. Paperwork can be manipulated. Numbers can be shifted. Especially by people who are as careful and vindictive as his mother and sister.

I mean, just think about it. When those little billing errors show up at work—and I'm talking about very specific transposition errors, things a seasoned clerk like me just doesn't make, not after doing this job day in and day out since I got my diploma—it's not a coincidence. Or when someone at church suddenly acts funny toward me... like Pastor Thomas looking right past me during the greeting last Sunday, or the ladies on the hospitality committee suddenly having their little private meetings without me. You can't put a bank statement over that and tell me it's not happening!

Misinterpreting? Doctor, with all due respect, are you even listening to a word I've been saying for the last twenty minutes? It feels like you're just asking the exact same question but using a thesaurus to find different words every time. First it was 'do I doubt it', then 'would I change my mind', and now 'am I misinterpreting' it. That is not a misinterpretation! When I go into my job, a job I've done perfectly well since high school, and those little billing errors keep showing up on the accounts I specifically manage... that's not me misinterpreting a simple typo. That is a targeted attack on my livelihood to make me look incompetent. 

And it's the exact same thing with my social life. When someone at church suddenly acts funny toward me, turning their back when I walk into the fellowship hall or whispering when I pass by the pews, I am not misreading their body language. I am a forty-seven-year-old woman, I have been going to that congregation for over a decade, and I know when I'm being shunned. People don't just change how they treat you overnight for no reason. 

So, no, I am not misinterpreting the signs. The signs are neon and flashing. And I know, I just know in my absolute core, that no matter what records anyone pulls up to try and convince me otherwise—whether it's the transaction logs at work or the monthly bank statements my husband keeps waving around—it all ties back to them. They are behind this. I am not misinterpreting anything, doctor, I am the only one actually seeing things clearly, and I just need someone to finally believe me instead of questioning my sanity.

Unshakeable? Contradictory evidence? Doctor, what you call "contradictory evidence" is exactly what I was talking about earlier! I feel like we are just going in circles today, I really do. I’m here because for months now—like I have already explained to you, at length—I’ve been trying to get people to understand that my husband’s family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. No. I know what I see with my own eyes. I know the extra work I have to do at my desk to fix what she breaks. 

So, yes. Call it unshakeable if you want to. But no matter what records anyone pulls up, no matter how much you try to contradict me, I know exactly who is doing this. I just need someone to finally stop arguing with me and actually do something about it.
